newsitem.title: USA: Gold price steadies after setting 20-month low.
newsitem.headline: Gold price steadies after setting 20-month low.

text.p: The price of gold steadied Tuesday as Wall Street's jitters over the stock market helped lift the precious metal from its lowest level in 20 months.

On New York's Commodity Exchange, December gold closed up 0.20 cent at $374.70 an ounce, rebounding from $373.20, which was its lowest level since March 3, 1995. It was also the first higher close after four straight sessions of losses.
In London, bullion was fixed at $373.50, the lowest since Jan. 9, 1995, and down $1 from the morning fixing.
Prior to the modest recovery in New York, sentiment was bearish in gold as investors shunned the precious metal in favour of soaring stock prices, analysts said.

Frenzied buying on Monday sparked the Dow Jones industrial average 73 points higher to 6,547.79, its 43rd record close this year as investors bet the slowing economy would help drive long-term interest rates lower.

But the mood in the stock market turned nervous Tuesday, as investors rushed to take profits. The Dow index lost 19.38 points to close at 6,528.41 after reversing an early gain of 40 points and trading briefly with a loss of slightly more than 50 points.
Analysts said fundamentals remains bearish for gold. Commodity funds are holding record short positions in gold futures, expecting even lower prices for the metal.
Also, hedging by South African and Australian gold producers is weighing on the market, with the price of gold having fallen sharply in Australian dollars and in South African rand.
